stories.title: Gears Of War: E-Day Estimated To Have Sold Just 320,000 Copies Despite Rave Reviews
stories.summary: But the Game Pass math is more complicated than you might think

sources.name: Kotaku
sources.title: Gears Of War: E-Day Estimated To Have Sold Just 320,000 Copies Despite Rave Reviews
sources.text: Gears of War: E-Day is the best-rated game in the series in a long time. But excellence is no predictor of market success these days, especially for a platform with as many competing business models as Xbox. According to data firm Alinea Analytics, Microsoft’s newest console-exclusive shooter sold just 320,000 copies in its first week, but had 1.7 million players on Game Pass. So is that good or bad for The Coalition, one of many Xbox game teams currently worried about future cuts ? “ Gears of War: E-Day has sold 230K copies,” Alinea’s Rhys Elliott posted on X on October 9, a week after the game’s early-access launch period began. “ Steam accounts for 168K of those, with Xbox (console and PC) selling 62K. But thereâs more to this story, as Xbox makes up the bulk of revenue (almost three-quarters).” He argues that Game Pass is cannibalizing much of the premium revenue fans might have spent on the game, without seemingly driving massive adoption from the rest of the subscriber-base, or some big uptick in the number of new sign-ups. Gears of War: E-Day has sold 230K copies ( @alineaanalytics estimates). Steam accounts for 168K of those, with Xbox (console and PC) selling 62K. But thereâs more to this story, as Xbox makes up the bulk of revenue (almost three-quarters). On Xbox, Game Pass is cannibalisingâ¦ pic.twitter.com/EH6GHFngYP — Rhys Elliott (@superhys) October 9, 2026 According to Alinea’s estimates, none of which have been corroborated by Microsoft, there were 1.7 million players who accessed E-Day via a Game Pass subscription instead of buying it, 722,000 of whom paid $30 for the Premium Edition upgrade to access the game early. Meanwhile, the game is estimated to have sold 230,000 copies so far, 168,000 of which were on Steam. That comes to roughly $37 million in revenue so far, $26 million of which came from players on Xbox. “In a world without day-one Game Pass, many of these folks would have bought E-Day at $70,” Elliott wrote. “ They paid $30 for five days early access to something they donât own. Xbox is, in effect, charging its most valuable customers the least, based on a hangover from a tried-and-exhausted strategy from a previous administration.” He notes that if the business model isn’t working for a game of the quality level that Gears of War: E-Day is at , then there clearly must be an issue with the business model. A cheap, ad-supported tier of Game Pass wouldn’t solve the problem of hardcore fans paying the least for access to a new exclusive, but increasing the price of day-one access might. The logical conclusion, based on Elliot’s estimates and analysis, is that Microsoft will have to remove day-one first-party releases from the service, just as it announced it would do earlier this year with Call of Duty . Donât miss the latest reviews, news and tips. Sign up for our free newsletter. Double Fine employees petitioned for a union in May. It created a rift in the studio that still hasn't healed And the former head of Minecraft is going to run it Halo: Campaign Evolved might be getting a horde mode as a skeleton crew works on one last update before Activision takes over the franchise Gears of War: E-Day including women commanders and soldiers is nothing new Battlefield 6 joins the subscription service this month, but so do a bunch of neat-looking indies Gears of War: E-Day is good, but will The Coalition get a chance to make more games before Xbox starts making cuts?

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Gears of War: E-Day reportedly courts over 1.7m Xbox Game Pass players and makes over $37m since launch
sources.text: Gears of War: E-Day's sales are reportedly lighter than you might expect from one of Xbox's flagship names, but pure sales numbers don't paint a complete picture of the bloody shooter's performance. A sizable chunk of revenue actually came from Game Pass subscribers paying for the game's Premium Edition upgrade. That's according to new estimates from Alinea Analytics' Rhys Elliott, which reports Xbox has sold around 230,000 copies of Gears of War: E-Day since the prequel's advance-access release at the very beginning of the month - with 168,000 of those sales coming from Steam and 62,000 coming from Xbox consoles and PC. Game Pass seemingly affected those stats to a large extent, like many other Xbox-published games this generation. Around 1.7m Locust-grinders played the shooter through their Game Pass subscription and more than 722,000 of them also bought the game's $30 Premium Edition upgrade. You see, owners of the Premium Edition that costs $99.99 were allowed to fend off the hordes early - from the 1st of October - but Game Pass subscribers could and still can drop a cheaper $30 for the Premium Edition upgrade and all its add-on extras. E-Day then launched in full for regular Game Pass subscribers and Standard Edition buyers on 6th October. When you include pure sales, microtransactions and those Premium Edition upgrades, Gears of War: E-Day has seemingly made above $37m (about £28m). As Alinea noted, almost a million people paid something for E-Day. "In a world without day-one Game Pass, many of these folks would have bought E-Day at $70," the analyst speculated. "They paid $30 for five days early access to something they don't own. Xbox is, in effect, charging its most valuable customers the least, based on a hangover from a tried-and-exhausted strategy from a previous administration." Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has already stopped new Call of Duty games from launching directly into the subscription service . With so much change afoot, it's not hard to imagine blockbuster games like Gears of War or Forza following suit. Another interesting tidbit comes from player overlap. On Xbox, more than 80% of E-Day players previously tried another Gears game, Call of Duty, Fortnite , GTA 5 and Halo Infinite . On Steam, 72% of players came from Counter-Strike and 65% of folks came from Helldivers 2 , which is probably unsurprising when you think about how similar E-Day's Horde Siege mode is to Arrowhead's PvE smash hit. Both have wide-open maps pulling you in all directions for side objectives and bug-like aliens to tear into chunks. The Coalition studio head Mike Crump recently claimed that E-Day is a "great foundation" for future sequels, and promised the next Gears won't "take nearly as long" to make after the seven-year gap between entries. With the game fully emerged, all eyes now turn to The Coalition - several people at the studio spoke to Eurogamer and feared post-launch layoffs could be on the horizon . "Gears of War: E-Day is a game of contrasts: conservative by its very nature, but with enough technical proficiency and iterative thinking to make its old-fashioned ideas feel competent and engaging," Eurogamer's Gears of War: E-Day review said. "Bleeding edge graphics with 20-year-old design sensibilities drip into this bloody crucible of familiarity that does nostalgia right."

sources.name: Polygon
sources.title: Gears of War: E-Day's Strong Reviews Haven't Translated to Big Sales, Analyst Says
sources.text: The numbers look good for Game Pass, but maybe not so good for Microsoft's bottom line Gears of War: E-Day is off to a strong critical start, but early sales estimates suggest Microsoft's latest Xbox blockbuster may be struggling to turn that acclaim into actual sales. The latest entry in The Coalition's third-person shooter series launched Oct. 6 on Xbox Series X and PC, returning players to the early days of the Locust invasion. But according to estimates from Alinea Analytics, the game sold just 230,000 copies during its early-access period, with most players instead accessing it through Xbox Game Pass. Alinea analyst Rhys Elliott shared the figures on X on Oct. 9, estimating that E-Day sold 168,000 copies on Steam and another 62,000 across Xbox console and PC. The game reportedly attracted 1.7 million Game Pass players, including an estimated 722,000 who paid $30 for the Premium Edition upgrade to play five days early. The numbers have not been confirmed by Microsoft, and they don't tell the whole story. Elliott noted that Xbox accounted for nearly three-quarters of the game's estimated revenue, despite Steam accounting for the majority of sales. Still, the figures raise questions about whether Game Pass is undermining Microsoft's ability to sell its biggest games at full price. “In a world without day-one Game Pass, many of these folks would have bought E-Day at $70,” Elliott wrote. “They paid $30 for five days early access to something they don't own.” The early sales estimates come despite a broadly positive critical reception. Gears of War: E-Day is tracking well, earning an 88 on Metacritic and an 87 on OpenCritic , making it the best-reviewed entries in the franchise in more than a decade. Polygon's review praised the prequel's combat, visuals, and emotional story about Marcus Fenix and Dominic Santiago during Emergence Day, calling it Gears at its finest despite some significant flaws. The review also highlighted the game's cinematic set pieces and detailed environments, though its lengthy campaign and sprawling open sections can drag. Elsewhere, IGN awarded the campaign a preliminary 9/10 , praising its emotional weight, while ScreenRant also gave it a 9/10 . PC Gamer, meanwhile, criticized the repetitive encounters and exhausting 20-plus-hour campaign, and GameSpot's in-progress review took issue with the game's reluctance to move beyond familiar series conventions . Those scores could also change. Critics initially reviewed the single-player campaign without access to the game's Horde Siege and multiplayer modes, leaving the full package's reception uncertain . For Microsoft, the bigger question may be whether strong reviews and millions of players translate into a sustainable business. E-Day appears to have found an audience on Game Pass , but Alinea's estimates suggest that audience may not be buying the game in the numbers Microsoft would hope for from one of its flagship franchises.

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: Gears of War E-Day sold just 62k copies on Xbox versus 1.7 million Game Pass players, analyst says
sources.text: But that "undersells the paying audience" of 722k Game Pass premium edition buyers Gears of War: E-Day sales topped 230,000 across Xbox and Steam following an October 1 launch, according to estimates from analyst firm Alinea. Market analysis head Rhys Elliott reports the Xbox player base is larger than it appears, even if premium sales were dominated by Steam. An estimated 62,000 people bought the game outright on Xbox consoles, with 168,000 buyers on Steam. SteamDB ownership estimates, which are always fallible and are especially volatile shortly after launch, support this figure, estimating 171,000 to 195,000 owners at the time of writing. How did a new, highly rated entry in a flagship series sell just 62,000 copies on Xbox in launch week? (Our Gears of War: E-Day review also awards it high marks.) Elliott notes that while Xbox Game Pass is "cannibalising much of the premium revenue," with some 1.7 million estimated players playing E-Day through the subscription service, over 722,000 Game Pass subs also paid for E-Day's premium upgrade. "So '230K copies' undersells the paying audience," Elliott writes. "Including the 722K upgrades, nearly 950K people actually paid something for E-Day." This brings the game's total estimated sales revenue to around $37 million. Nevertheless, "The $70 premium SKU is – functionally – dead on Xbox," Elliott argues. I've reached out to Microsoft for comment on these figures, which remain unconfirmed estimates, and its expectations for E-Day. Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more As Circana games analyst Mat Piscatella points out online (not in direct response to Alinea's report, but certainly in its orbit), "it isn't straight cannibalism if a person paying for Game Pass plays an offered game through the service." Many game developers, including several who've worked with or under Microsoft, have criticized the effects Game Pass can have on full-fat sales or the value of games. This year, Microsoft removed new Call of Duty games from the service's day-one offerings, though it stopped short of admitting it was losing too much money on the deal as Game Pass growth failed to meet expectations despite a significant bump from CoD. However, the assumption that, in a world without Xbox Game Pass, the sales of games like Gears of War: E-Day would be directly boosted by however large their Game Pass audience was doesn't hold up. "Not every person who plays a game via a sub service would buy that game were it not included in that service," Piscatella notes. We don't, and can't, know exactly how many Game Pass players, or even Game Pass premium upgraders, would've paid full price in this case, but it certainly wouldn't be all of them. We also can't separate the value of any Game Pass subscriptions purchased by people enticed by E-Day – that is, the value-add. E-Day was once on track to become another multiplatform Xbox game before Microsoft shelved a reportedly near-finished PS5 port to prioritize its home console, even if that means limiting its audience. Gears of War: E-Day studio reportedly fears post-launch layoffs, "wouldn't put it past" Microsoft to withhold bonuses . Austin has been a game journalist for 12 years, having freelanced for the likes of PC Gamer, Eurogamer, IGN, Sports Illustrated, and more while finishing his journalism degree. He's been with GamesRadar+ since 2019. They've yet to realize his position is a cover for his career-spanning Destiny column, and he's kept the ruse going with a lot of news and the occasional feature, all while playing as many roguelikes as possible. sources.name: Xbox Wire
sources.title: DMZ — 5 Features to Get Excited for in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4’s New Mode
sources.text: Call of Duty’s upcoming DMZ mode sounds like it’s shaping up to be something special. Set on the new Haijin map and inspired by the events and locations from Modern Warfare 4 ’s Campaign, this open-world combat environment will challenge you to loot, complete objectives, fight both enemies and rival Operators, and extract before everything you’ve earned is lost. Recent intel drops on the official Call of Duty Blog have given us a much clearer picture of what awaits in Haijin when DMZ launches as part of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 . Players who have digitally pre-ordered or pre-purchased Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 can gain Early Access to the game’s Campaign starting Friday, October 16 and all of DMZ starting Tuesday, October 20. The events within DMZ are set after the main MW4 Campaign, leaving a power vacuum in its wake. Now it’s up to you to identify a new, mysterious threat and dismantle its operations across the DMZ through various deployments. From scavenging for crafting materials and experimenting with new technology, to leveling up an Operator, the mode sounds like it offers plenty to look forward to. Here are five features to get excited for when you begin your deployment. The 3D Printer will be available back at the Forward Operating Base (FOB) between deployments and will serve as your primary crafting station to build equipment and upgrades for your loadout before you drop into Haijin. The Call of Duty Blog shares that , as you progress through the DMZ, you’ll unlock new crafting recipes to create more powerful equipment – as well as upgrades to the 3D Printer and even the Forward Operating Base itself. Recipes can also be found on deployments and, presuming you extract in one piece, you can then craft those items for your Operator back at the FOB. When focused on crafting new equipment, the two key things you’ll be looking for when looting on deployments will be Resources and 3D Printer Ingredients – these are the two types of main elements to craft all items. There are four basic Resources to find during a deployment: Synthetics, Electronics, Chemicals, and Metals, automatically broken down from looted items, into your Backpack and Stash. 3D Printer Ingredients are rarer materials found in specific areas of Haijin and are valuable as an ingredient to make a new Item. Examples include Binding Catalyst, Biomaterials, Detonators, and Control Units, to name a few. Once you have enough of these two types of materials, you can select how many copies of an item you want to craft at once, then choose where crafted items go: send completed items directly to your Stash for later or equip them directly to your Operator to quickly prepare for the next deployment. Having this flexibility in how you want to engage the enemy during your deployment can open a variety of experiences in DMZ and can make each deployment feel like it matters, even if you come back to the FOB with zero kills to your name – at least you’ve got handful of electronics or a comms module to make it worth your time. Extraction shooters are always more engaging when every deployment has a clear purpose. That’s not going to be problem with DMZ as it will offer three ways to deploy: Story Missions, Dynamic Operations, and Free Roam. Of those, Story Missions and Dynamic Operations are two that really stand out with their defined objectives and high-tier rewards. According to the Call of Duty Blog , Story Missions will feature narrative-led deployments that you can complete and replay, though some remain locked until prerequisites are met. Each entry provides briefing intel, required objectives, and rewards – usually high-value gear and DMZ Cash – along with options for a random mission and additional milestone rewards. Dynamic Operations, meanwhile, give squads multiple goals to pursue within the DMZ. After deploying, you choose an operation and complete its objectives to earn DMZ XP, Cash, and the ability to call in a Supply Drop filled with unpredictable loot. That extra payoff adds anticipation to every successful Op while making Dynamic Operations a promising source of both Cash and XP. Persistent Operators may be DMZ’s most exciting feature because they allow Haijin to leave a lasting mark on you. You’ll begin with two Operator slots, and unlock a third as you progress through DMZ levels. Each Operator then grows stronger by surviving deployments and earning DMZ XP. Each successful exfil levels up your Operator’s Dog Tags, and this is the key to gaining Trait Points for your Operator. You can invest those points across the Warfighter, Scout, and Survivalist Trait Trees, creating a meaningful choice between specialization and flexibility: with a maximum of 18 points to earn, and a choice of over 60 Trait Points to augment your Operator, you can tailor each Operator to your skills and preferred role. For example, Warfighter Traits include Combat Resistance, Quick Fix, and Viper Sense; Scout Traits include improved Thermal Padding, UAV Upgrade, and Field Crafting; while Survivalist Traits include Faster and Free Revives, increased Consumable Duration, and many more. But here’s where it gets dicey: if an Operator fails to extract and becomes MIA, you must either recover them with DMZ Cash or dismiss them. Because recovery costs rise with Trait investment, bringing back a high-level Operator becomes increasingly expensive. Recovered Operators keep their Traits but lose their gear, putting real weight behind every deployment. The chase for loot is at the heart of every extraction shooter, and DMZ makes each haul matter beyond the current deployment. Returning to base with a pack full of supplies doesn’t just feel rewarding – it improves your chances of success the next time you enter Hajin. Once you drop into a deployment, looting should be a top priority. Searching containers provides resources for combat, supports marked Operations, strengthens your position in Hajin, and offers a reliable way to earn DMZ XP and

sources.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Launch Rollout Adds DMZ Early Access
sources.text: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has added DMZ to its list of early access experiences available for pre-order players ahead of its launch later this month. Activision and Infinity Ward revealed a host of new details for its DMZ revamp in a blog post shared today. Early access for the mode joins campaign early access , with both available to those who pre-ordered either the standard or Vault Edition versions of the game across PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and/or Xbox Series X/S. Here's the full breakdown: Eligible players will gain early access to the Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 campaign starting Friday, October 16. DMZ early access will then follow Tuesday, October 20, with the full launch unleashing the rest of the experience come Friday, October 23. All of the new details arrived with a new gameplay trailer for DMZ, which you can see below. DMZ was first introduced as Call of Duty's take on the extraction shooter experience with 2022's Modern Warfare 2 . It was expanded upon in the months that followed but was ultimately deemed to be an underwhelming prototype by many. Support ended in late 2023, and now, Activision is taking another swing at it. The DMZ in Modern Warfare 4 has been propped up as a fully fleshed-out evolution for the game mode. In today's post, Infinity Ward described the new take on the mode as the series' "definitive extraction shooter experience," promising persistent progression in the open-world combat environment known as the Hajin Exclusion Zone. "There's an interesting story with the DMZ beta, where we had to make some decisions," studio multiplayer creative director Joe Cecot said in a recent behind-the-scenes video (below). "Certain things we wanted to do, we couldn't do. At the end of the day, we learned a lot: That we made a very approachable, fun sandbox that was fun to fight in, to explore, to make friends in, to get into fights in. There's a bunch of stuff we left on the table, so as soon as we finished with the last game, we were just gung-ho on, 'OK, we know what we want to do.'" Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launches October 23 for PC and consoles. Our first proper look at DMZ gameplay arrived in June, with even more details shared earlier this week. While early access players will get to dive into DMZ and the story mode a few days earlier than others, core multiplayer offerings won't officially launch until that firm release date hits. You can see how the team at Infinity Ward is working to deal with wall-hack cheaters here . Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

sources.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 DMZ Early Access Announced
sources.text: Players who want to dive into DMZ in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 will be able to do so earlier than other parts of the game. Activision has announced that Modern Warfare 4: DMZ will release in Early Access on October 20. That’s three days prior to the October 23 launch of the full game. Campaign early access is still days earlier, on October 16. In order to get early access to the new DMZ, players simply have to pre-order or pre-purchase Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. It doesn’t matter what version of the game or platform. All players are eligible. DMZ is Call of Duty’s extraction shooter mode that’s returning after first appearing in 2022. “You’re free to explore, engage AI forces and rival Operators, loot valuable items, craft gear, and complete objectives— all while keeping your eye on the final exfil, extracting with your rewards at the end of each deployment. How you approach each deployment, within a squad or acting alone, is entirely up to you,” Activision says. Are you going to pre-order Modern Warfare 4 to get early access to DMZ? sources.name: Gematsu
sources.title: DAVE THE DIVER DLC ‘Subnautica 2 Content Pack’ announced
sources.text: MINTROCKET has announced DAVE THE DIVER ‘s final downloadable content pack—a Subnautica 2 -themed expansion in partnership with Unknown Worlds Entertainment . It will launch free of charge in early 2027. “For our final [downloadable content] expansion, we wanted to create something that felt especially meaningful, and a Subnautica collaboration is what players have been asking us about for a long time,” said MINTROCKET studio director Jaeho Hwang in a press release. “Both games are set underwater, but Subnautica has such a distinct approach to underwater exploration, so working with the Subnautica 2 team gave us a chance to bring a new wave to DAVE THE DIVER experience. We’re really excited for players to see what we’ve been working on, and we hope this collaboration gives them one more fresh and surprising adventure with Dave and his friends, old and new.” Subnautica 2 creative director Anthony Gallegos added, “We’re so excited to collaborate with the team at MINTROCKET. It’s clear that we both adore one another’s games a lot, and the expansion is a love letter to both DAVE THE DIVER and the Subnautica universe. People are in for a treat.” The free expansion will see players explore the strange new waters of Proteus, filled with unfamiliar creatures and valuable resources waiting to be discovered. The upcoming Subnautica 2 Content Pack creates a confluence of mysterious waters unlike anything before, with Dave and Bancho traveling interdimensionally to make new discoveries, unlock strange and exotic recipes, and lend a hand to new friends in need—all while facing periodic confrontations with the perilous Leviathan. DAVE THE DIVER is available now for PlayStation 5 , Xbox Series , Switch 2 , PlayStation 4 , Xbox One , Switch , PC via Steam , Epic Games Store , and Microsoft Store , iOS, and Android.

sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: Subnautica 2 fans can finally hunt and kill those pesky Nibbler Mangos—in Dave the Diver's crossover DLC
sources.text: I will kill them. I will cook them. I will serve them. Thanks, Dave. It took a while but there's finally an official way to hunt and kill some of Subnautica 2's most annoying sea creatures. The only catch is, you'll have to do it in Dave the Diver DLC—though as catches go, that's a pretty fun one. The crossover was announced today at the Triple-I Initiative showcase. Coming in early 2027, the Dave the Diver X Subnautica 2 content pack will suck Dave into the alien waters of Unknown Worlds' survival game where he can mine resources, hunt fish, and—one would hope—discover some tasty new sushi recipes for Bancho to cook up. Here's the trailer: What caught my eye even more than the glimpse of a massive and intimidating boss at the end of the trailer were those pesky Nibbler Mangos, which start biting you the second you dive into Subnautica 2 and never really stop. Players having no way to kill large enemies in Subnautica 2 has been a bit of a controversy , with some even resorting to mods so they can fight back. It's nice that players can finally get a bit of revenge against those relentless fish, albeit in another game. "We're thrilled to see Subnautica 2's creatures, including the Nibbler Mango, join Dave's world," Mintrocket told PC Gamer via email. "The team had a lot of fun bringing these creatures into our game, and players can expect the DLC to play just like the Dave the Diver they know and love." As for those saddened to hear this is the final DLC for Dave the Diver, that doesn't necessarily mean it's the definitive end of his adventures. "While this will be the final major DLC for Dave the Diver, there may still be smaller content updates or collaborations based on player feedback and our internal plans," Mintrocket told PC Gamer. "Since we're not moving straight into a sequel, we'll keep thinking about ways to make sure players don't forget Dave and his friends." Bancho the Chef, meanwhile, is getting his own game , a prequel, though a release date has yet to be announced. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. Chris started playing PC games in the 1980s, started writing about them in the early 2000s, and (finally) started getting paid to write about them in the late 2000s. Following a few years as a regular freelancer, PC Gamer hired him in 2014, probably so he'd stop emailing them asking for more work. Chris has a love-hate relationship with survival games and an unhealthy fascination with the inner lives of NPCs. He's also a fan of offbeat simulation games, mods, and ignoring storylines in RPGs so he can make up his own. sources.title: Live-action Cyberpunk 2077 film reportedly in development, with CD Projekt Red collaborating with Paramount to make it
sources.text: UPDATE 12PM BST: CD Projekt Red seems to have confirmed the partnership and film, with joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski commenting on X that: "We're excited about Paramount as a future partner who shares our creative ambitions for the Cyberpunk franchise. We look forward to sharing more details at the appropriate time." ORIGINAL STORY 11:40AM BST: A live-action Cyberpunk 2077 film is reportedly in the works at Paramount Pictures. Producer Lorenzo di Bonaventura - a former Warner Bros. exec influential in signing the The Matrix and Harry Potter films, and known for producing the Transformers films - is said to be attached to the project, with CD Projekt Red collaborating. The report comes from Deadline , though the publication had no further information to share than what's above. CD Projekt Red told us it doens't have anything to share beyond what Nowakowski said on X. Believing that CD Projekt Red would venture into live-action film territory doesn't take a stretch of the imagination. The company's Netflix anime partnership on Cyberpunk Edgerunners has been a success, with a second series due to air this month, on 20th October . The first season, released in 2022, was "fantastic", Wes wrote in his Cyberpunk Edgerunners impressions article , and amassed considerable Netflix viewing figures . Live-action adaptations of video game-based series are also becoming increasingly popular, with The Last of Us and Fallout particularly finding wide success. CD Projekt Red being involved with the Cyberpunk 2077 adaptation would also somewhat heal a wound left by not being involved with The Witcher Netflix adaptation. CD Projekt art director Pawel Mileniczuk called this a "missed opportunity" when I talked to him for a Witcher 3 10-year anniversary article last year. Meanwhile, CD Projekt Red is working on Cyberpunk 2 , a project that's in pre-production, but with an expanding team - close to 200 people as of 31st July 2026 - full production doesn't seem far away. The sequel apparently adds a second city alongside the iconic Night City setting, and it's described as being like "Chicago gone wrong". Should the live-action film prove real, and be made, the questions are what story will it tell - the same as in Cyberpunk 2077? - and which actors will play the game's well-known roles? The most famous of those roles is Keanu Reeves' portrayal of Johnny Silverhand, a character who used Reeves' likeness in the game. Could Reeves star in a film adaptation? Cyberpunk 2077 was released in 2021 , and its rocky launch has since become infamous. But CD Projekt Red did extensive work improving the game after release, focusing its efforts around a kind of 2.0 relaunch alongside the game's "remarkable" Phantom Liberty expansion , in 2023. Paramount, meanwhile, recently acquired Warner Bros., and has since reorganised into mega-company Skydance. Activision's former leader Bobby Kotick has been employed on the board of it .

sources.title: Ghost of Tsushima: Legends anime delayed to 2028
sources.text: The anime series based on the Sucker Punch Productions -developed PlayStation game Ghost of Tsushima: Legends , which was previously planned to debut in 2027, which will now premiere on Crunchyroll in 2028, Aniplex and Crunchyroll announced . Mayumi Saco and Shinya Fukumatsu will join the cast of the show in undisclosed role. Saco previously voiced Tomoe in the original game, while while Fukumatsu is known for portraying Bomb in One-Punch Man . The anime is being directed by Takanobu Mizuno at studio Kamikaze Douga, with Gen Urobuchi writing the story composition and co-writing the script with Renji Oki. New staff members include composer Keiji Inai, sound director Yoshikazu Iwanami, sound editor Yasumasa Koyama, and title calligraphy artist Gyousyou Suzuki. Ghost of Tsushima: Legends is produced by HAYATE in collaboration with Aniplex and PlayStation Productions, with Sony Music serving as music and soundtrack partner.

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: Ghost of Tsushima anime arrives in 2028 as OG game actor joins cast
sources.text: Ghost of Tsushima Legends has been delayed The upcoming Ghost of Tsushima anime has received a disappointing release date update alongside news of new cast and behind-the-scenes arrivals. At New York Comic Con, Crunchyroll revealed that Ghost of Tsushima Legends is now set for 2028, a slight pushback from its original 2027 window. Two actors, Mayumi Skco and Shinya Fukumatsu, were also confirmed to join the cast. If you've played Ghost of Tsushima in Japanese, you may recognize Saco's voice – she portrayed turncoat villain Tomoe in 2020's Ghost of Tsushima game. It is unknown who the pair will be portraying in Legends, however. Ghost of Tsushima is a 2020 open world adventure charting the revenge journey of Jin Sakai on the Japanese island of Tsushima during feudal times. It was followed up in 2024 by Ghost of Yotei, offering players a new quest as the katana-wielding Atsu hunted down the fearsome Yotei Six after the murder of her parents. In truth, we probably should have expected the delay. We've heard precious little about Ghost of Tsushima Legends since its announcement way back in January 2025. "The Ghost of Tsushima anime will offer fans an exciting new way to experience the game in an anime style that will be bold and groundbreaking," Crunchyroll president Rahul Purini, said at the time in a statement. PlayStation Productions head Asad Qizilbash added, "Ghost of Tsushima’s rich, immersive world and its fantastical Legends mode based on Japanese mythology provide the perfect canvas for this project, and Aniplex is the perfect partner to translate Sucker Punch Productions’ hit video game into a stunning new anime series."
